newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU docks farm funds to recoup 1993 irregularities.
newsitem.headline: EU docks farm funds to recoup 1993 irregularities.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it would dock 539 million ecus from member states' farm budgets to penalise them for irregularities in 1993.
The Commission said in a statement that there had been "serious deficiencies" and possible fraud by member states in checking export refunds on farm products such as olive oil.
In its clearance of accounts for the 1993 financial year, the Commission approved farm spending of close to 32 billion ecus, but put off a decision on a further 120 million ecus.
The clearance of accounts system allows the European Union to recover money paid out "without sufficient guarantees as to the legitimacy or proper control and verification of payments".

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said that control of Common Agriculture Policy spending was the responsibility of member states and that the Commission would not hesitate in penalising those who failed to check how EU taxpayers' money was spent.
The Commission said that over half the amount rejected related to Italy, Spain and Greece flouting EU milk quota laws.

For the rest, it said that France, Germany, Belgium, Italy and the Netherlands were at fault in not properly checking prefinanced export refunds, while Spain and Greece were too lax, allowing irregularities to happen.
Greece was also singled out for failing to set up a register of olive trees used to verify payments of production aid, while Italy and Portugal failed to control olive oil consumption aid.

The Commission said it found insufficient control over public storage of cereals in Italy, France and Greece, while Italy, France, Ireland, Portugal and Spain also failed to apply controls over livestock premia.
Germany and Italy were penalised over sugar rules.

France and Italy also failed to distill sufficient quantities of surplus wine, while Italy and Greece were too slow in recovering tobacco premia. Britain was found to have accepted irregular tenders for beef sales into public storage.
The Commission said it had carried out over 150 spot-checks relating to 1993 spending. "The clearance (of accounts) plays an effective preventative role in the fight against fraud..," it said.
